dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real n-by-n matrix A, real vector x, and index i in Fin n, this is the finite sum sum_{j in Fin n} |A(i,j)| |x(j)|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to Ainv and q, it gives the exact nonnegative row sum sum_j |Ainv(i,j)| |q(j)| appearing in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a real n-by-n matrix A, real vector x, and index i in Fin n, this is the finite sum sum_{j in Fin n} A(i,j) x(j), namely component i of the matrix-vector product Ax.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to Ainv and q, it is the matrix-vector-product component used in both the exact update equation and the bound on h.

binders: n is an arbitrary natural number.
Ainv is an arbitrary real n-by-n matrix, represented as a function Fin n -> Fin n -> R.
x, q, h, and xNext are arbitrary real vectors indexed by Fin n.
u is an arbitrary real number.
The conclusion is asserted for every component index i in Fin n.
hypotheses: The parameter u is nonnegative: 0 <= u.
For every i in Fin n, xNext(i) = (sum_{j in Fin n} Ainv(i,j) q(j)) + x(i) + h(i).
For every i in Fin n, |h(i)| <= u |sum_{j in Fin n} Ainv(i,j) q(j)| + u |x(i)|.
conclusions: For every i in Fin n, |xNext(i) - x(i)| <= (1 + u) sum_{j in Fin n} |Ainv(i,j)| |q(j)| + u |x(i)|.
mathematical_definitions: Let I_n = Fin n, the set of indices 0,1,...,n-1.
Define r_i = sum_{j in I_n} Ainv(i,j) q(j), the i-th component of the matrix-vector product Ainv q.
Define s_i = sum_{j in I_n} |Ainv(i,j)| |q(j)|, the i-th component of the product of the entrywise absolute matrix |Ainv| with the entrywise absolute vector |q|.
All sums are finite sums over every j in Fin n; when n = 0, such sums equal zero.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural dimension n, every real n-by-n matrix Ainv, real vectors x, q, h, and xNext of length n, and nonnegative real u, suppose componentwise that xNext is obtained by adding x, the matrix-vector product Ainv q, and h, and that |h(i)| is at most u times the magnitude of (Ainv q)(i) plus u times |x(i)|. Then, for every component i, the magnitude of the change xNext(i) - x(i) is at most (1 + u) times sum_j |Ainv(i,j)| |q(j)| plus u |x(i)|.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The name Ainv imposes no mathematical condition: the proposition does not state that Ainv is invertible or is the inverse of another matrix.
Only u >= 0 is assumed; there is no upper bound such as u < 1.
The result is componentwise and uses ordinary scalar absolute values. It is not a vector-norm or matrix-norm inequality.
The quantity sum_j |Ainv(i,j)| |q(j)| is an exact finite weighted absolute row sum, not the absolute value of the signed sum.
No relation between x and q is assumed beyond their appearance in the update and perturbation hypotheses.
The proposition does not encode a floating-point type, rounding operation, algorithm, or relative-error model beyond the explicit assumed bound on h.
The update equation is exact; h is an additive term constrained only by the stated componentwise bound.
When n = 0, Fin n has no indices, so both indexed hypotheses and the indexed conclusion are vacuous.
For choices of xNext and h that do not satisfy the update or perturbation hypotheses, the conditional proposition imposes no conclusion.
There are no existential quantifiers or witness choices; all data and component indices are universally quantified.
